newsitem.title: THAILAND: THAI PACKAGE NOT FOR FINANCE SECTOR BAILOUT - IMF.
newsitem.headline: THAI PACKAGE NOT FOR FINANCE SECTOR BAILOUT - IMF.

text.p: Thailand must not use its new $16 billion loan package to bail out the country's ailing finance sector, an International Monetary Fund (IMF) official said on Wednesday.

"It will be used to cover financial payments, for example, if the balance of payments is not covered by the longterm capital this money can be used as and when necessary. The fund will absolutely not be used to clean up the finance sector," Hubert Neiss, director of the IMF's Asia and Pacific Department and head of an IMF team to Bangkok, told a news conference.
Neiss said that Thai authorities and the IMF team had on Wednesday completed their work for a comprehensive policy package that could be the basis of an IMF-supported programme.

"The agreed policy package will now be reviewed by IMF management and it is my expectation that the proposed economic programme will be submitted expeditiously to the IMF executive board for final approval," he said.
"Once approval is obtained disbursement for the financial package arranged in Tokyo will begin immediately," he added.
Details of the agreed programme were not immediately available.
The IMF earlier indicated it wanted a tough set of measures including a floating exchange rate, rapid action on effectively insolvent financial companies and a balanced budget.
